sections.h2: Where does Beavercreek fit in the Dayton area?
sections.html:
Beavercreek is the largest city in Greene County and lies about five miles east of downtown Dayton, so many of its homes sit within a short drive of Dayton jobs. Census estimates put the city at 48,134 residents for 2025, spread over about 26.6 square miles of land.

Settlers arrived in the early 1800s, and part of Beavercreek Township incorporated as a city in February 1980. The city absorbed the former communities of Alpha, Knollwood, most of New Germany and Zimmerman, and an older deed may use one of those names. The legal description and parcel number in your deed matter more to a title company than the neighborhood label.

Growth has been gradual. Wikipedia's census table lists 37,984 residents in 2000, 45,193 in 2010 and 46,549 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate of 48,134 is about 3% above the 2020 base. A mayor elected directly by voters and six at-large council members run the city, with a city manager appointed by council, and public meetings air on the city's cable channel.

sections.h2: How do Beavercreek housing numbers compare with Lorain County suburbs?
sections.html:
Beavercreek has a larger renter share than Avon Lake or Avon. In the 2020 to 2024 data, 71.8% of homes are owner-occupied, the median home value is $279,600 and the median rent is $1,457. The city has 19,453 households averaging 2.39 people, and monthly owner costs are $1,837 with a mortgage and $838 without.

  • The 2020 census counted 19,980 housing units, 5.3% of them vacant.
  • Among occupied units, 72.6% were owner-occupied and 27.4% rented.
  • The median age was 40.6, and 20.0% of residents were 65 or older.

More than a quarter of occupied homes are rented, so landlords and renters make up part of the demand. A homeowner with a long repair list can ask a direct buyer about an as-is purchase instead of renovating first.

sections.h2: Which Beavercreek permits and registrations come up at sale?
sections.html:
Permits split between the city and the county. The city's Planning and Development Department issues zoning permits, and Greene County Building Regulation handles building, plumbing, electrical and HVAC permits. The table lists the permit the city names for common projects, which helps you spot open work before a buyer's inspector does.

Permit that Beavercreek lists for common residential projects
ProjectPermit or office
New house, addition or attached garageResidential Zoning Permit
DeckResidential Zoning Permit
Swimming poolSwimming Pool Permit
Shed or detached garage, propane tankAccessory Structure Permit
Fence or retaining wallFence Permit
Interior remodel such as wall removal or a finished basementGreene County Building Regulation, no zoning permit
Abandoned, foreclosure or vacant propertyRegistration Application

Sources: beavercreekohio.gov.

Zoning permits are not required for interior remodeling, at-grade patios, garage sales or driveways. Applications run through the online permit center, and printed forms can be filed at City Hall on Research Park Drive. If the house is vacant, ask the planning office whether the registration rule applies to it.

  • Greene County Building Regulation, at 667 Dayton-Xenia Road in Xenia, issues building, plumbing, electrical and HVAC permits.
  • Greene County Public Health, at 360 Wilson Drive in Xenia, is the county contact for health department questions.
  • Greene County Sanitary Engineering, at the same Dayton-Xenia Road address, is the contact for sewer questions.
  • The Beavercreek Fire Department is at 851 N. Orchard Lane.

sections.h2: Are short-term rentals allowed in Beavercreek?
sections.html:
They are, with a city license. Ordinance 23-15 and Chapter 117 of the city code require every owner to apply through the Online Permit Center before renting for fewer than thirty consecutive days. A license lasts two years and must be renewed.

  • The application lists the location, where the unit will be advertised, bedrooms, maximum occupants, parking and emergency contacts.
  • Renters must be at least 25 years old, and owners must hand them house rules, noise rules and emergency details.
  • The city's 3% hotel, motel and short-term rental tax is filed quarterly, even for quarters with no rentals.

Owners inside a homeowners association should read its covenants first, as the city advises. For a house that has run as a rental, tell buyers about the license and the tax filings, and ask the planning office whether a new owner must file a fresh application.

sections.h2: How does Greene County process a Beavercreek deed?
sections.html:
The Greene County Auditor transfers the deed, and the recorder files it afterward. The auditor requires a completed Real Property Conveyance Statement of Value and Receipt (form DTE 100), and the grantor's name must match how the grantor took title in the previous deed. The county map department must approve the deed before it reaches the auditor, and land in the farmland tax program needs the DTE 101 statement.

The auditor's page prints the cost this way: a transfer tax of fifty cents per parcel and a conveyance fee of $2 for every thousand dollars of the sale price, rounded up to the nearest $100. The county offers an online calculator. The recorder's standards add a complete legal description with the parcel number, a prepared-by statement, the prior deed reference and a notarial acknowledgment.

sections.h2: How are Greene County property taxes handled for a sale?
sections.html:
The county auditor appraises each parcel at fair market value every six years and updates values every three. The auditor's office is at 69 Greene Street in Xenia, and its appraisers will talk through a valuation or start an appeal. Property taxes fund schools, public safety, roads, libraries and parks.

Due dates move with state changes. For the second half of 2026, the Greene County Treasurer announced that the House Bill 186 inflation cap credit delayed bills, and that the Tax Commissioner approved a payment due date of Friday, August 14, 2026. Escrow borrowers had no action to take. For your own closing year, ask the treasurer for the schedule and have the title company prorate the tax between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What do Beavercreek schools, parks and transit mean for buyers?
sections.html:
Beavercreek City School District has one preschool, six elementary schools, two middle schools, a Freshman School and Beavercreek High School. The parks department maintains 24 parks and properties, and Beavercreek Station is a hub on Creekside Trail, which runs from Xenia to Eastwood MetroPark in Dayton. The Greater Dayton Regional Transit Authority runs bus service in the city, and the public library is a branch of the Greene County Public Library.

These details help a listing, and they also tell a direct buyer what the house is worth to the next owner. If you sell as is, ask the buyer to state in writing that repairs are theirs, and keep a copy of any inspection report you ordered.

faqs.q: Do I need a city permit to sell a house in Beavercreek?
faqs.a: The city's permit list covers construction work, short-term rental licenses and registration of vacant or foreclosure properties. Check for open permits on past work, since decks, pools, fences and sheds need zoning permits and the county handles building, plumbing, electrical and HVAC permits.

faqs.q: What fees does Greene County charge on a deed?
faqs.a: The auditor's page lists a transfer tax of fifty cents per parcel and a conveyance fee of $2 per thousand dollars of the sale price, rounded up to the nearest $100. The county's online calculator shows the amount for your sale.

faqs.q: Can a Beavercreek short-term rental license pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: Ask the planning office. Licenses last two years and go to the owner who applies, so a new owner may need to file a new application through the Online Permit Center.

faqs.q: When are Greene County taxes due?
faqs.a: Dates are set each year. The second half of 2026 was due Friday, August 14, 2026, after a delay tied to House Bill 186. Ask the Greene County Treasurer for the schedule that matches your closing.

faqs.q: What must I disclose when I sell my Beavercreek home?
faqs.a: Complete the Ohio property disclosure form if the home has up to four units. ORC 5302.30 lists exceptions such as estate sales and transfers to relatives, and the signed deed must be acknowledged before a notary under ORC 5301.01.
